note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute progressive upper lip swelling and difficulty breathing after eating prawn soup.
- Onset/duration/progression: Ate prawn soup at ~19:00; lip symptoms began approximately 30 minutes afterwards and have been increasing in size since onset.
- Associated symptoms: Reported difficulty breathing and lightheadedness/dizziness. No documentation of rash, vomiting, or tongue/throat exam findings in transcript.
- Context/previous episodes: Patient reports a similar episode ~1 year ago after a late meal (possible curry) with facial swelling and breathing difficulty on waking. Patient has a lifelong peanut allergy.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (uses salbutamol inhaler; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Peanut allergy (history since childhood).
- Childhood severe allergic reaction: patient recalls receiving an injection as a child per mother’s recollection (details not documented).
- Medications: Salbutamol inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented. Patient sometimes takes antihistamines but specific agent and dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Peanut allergy noted; no details about epinephrine autoinjector availability documented.

Physical Examination:
- Reported findings: Progressive swelling of the upper lip (initially left corner), worsening in size; patient reports difficulty breathing and dizziness.
- Observations: Patient was able to converse but became increasingly distressed and lightheaded during the consult.
- Relevant negatives/unknowns: No explicit documentation of tongue swelling, visible throat swelling, urticaria, stridor, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, heart rate, blood pressure, or formal airway exam. No antihistamines on person at time of consult.

Impression:
- Suspected anaphylactic/allergic reaction temporally related to ingestion of prawn soup with progressive lip swelling and respiratory compromise.

Management Plan:
- Immediate actions advised/taken:
  - Clinician advised emergency ambulance activation and indicated intention to call ambulance.
  - Patient/attending family asked to call emergency services (999) for suspected anaphylaxis; family agreed to call.
  - Instructed patient to take available oral antihistamine immediately while waiting for emergency services.
- Further recommendations given:
  - Attend hospital/emergency services for urgent assessment and management.
  - After hospital treatment, contact the clinic to arrange discussion regarding possible epinephrine autoinjector and allergy follow-up.

Patient Summary:
- Patient developed progressive upper lip swelling, shortness of breath, and dizziness approximately 30 minutes after eating prawn soup. This is suspected to represent an anaphylactic or severe allergic reaction. Emergency services were contacted/being arranged and patient was advised to take antihistamine while awaiting ambulance and to proceed to hospital for urgent care; follow-up arranged to consider epinephrine/autoinjector.

Key Takeaways:
- Call emergency services immediately for suspected anaphylaxis (999).
- Take any available oral antihistamine immediately while waiting for emergency services.
- Proceed to hospital for urgent assessment and possible treatment; arrange follow-up afterward for consideration of epinephrine autoinjector.

Next Steps:
- Emergency medical services evaluation and transport to hospital for acute management.
- In-hospital assessment/treatment (not specified in transcript).
- Post-discharge follow-up with clinician to arrange review and consideration of epinephrine autoinjector and allergy referral.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: current vital signs (respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, heart rate, blood pressure, temperature); formal airway and cardio/respiratory physical exam findings; confirmation of whether clinician actually completed ambulance call; details of prior allergic reaction(s) (dates, treatment received, hospitalizations); current list of all medications including regular asthma preventer inhalers; status of epinephrine autoinjector availability.
- Conflicts/uncertainties from transcript: Patient uncertain which antihistamines she sometimes takes; childhood injection for allergy is recalled second-hand (mother reported) and lacks documentation. No direct confirmation whether antihistamines were actually taken before ambulance arrival.
- Transcript quality comment: Overall intelligible; patient became increasingly distressed and intermittently inaudible at moments. Some medication and place names not specified.
